$comment: Phase-2 wave-2 OpenConnector ingestion config for AusTender (Australian federal procurement, api.tenders.gov.au OCDS API). Mirrors concurrentie-analyse/scripts/sync/sync_australia_austender.py's endpoint + field selection. Public, unauthenticated OCDS release feed (no key, no OAuth - confirmed by reading the script: only a User-Agent/Accept header, no os.environ credential anywhere). Engine path: plain OCDS JSON (json_decode, no gzip/XML/POST needed). The date-range endpoint `findByDates/contractPublished/{start}/{end}` takes ISO-8601 start/end in the URL PATH (not query params); the endpoint template below computes 'last 7 days' fresh on every run via self-contained Twig date expressions (same object-independent pattern latvia_iub.json/estonia_rhr.json use for their date-scoped endpoints - MappingService/SynchronizationService fall through to Twig whenever the template contains {{ }}). Response envelope: `{"releases": [...]}` (resultsPosition: 'releases'), each release OCDS-shaped (ocid, tender.*, buyer.*, awards[], contracts[]). Faithful-mapping caveats vs the Python script (documented, confirmed live 2026-07-07, not forced): (1) the `findByDates/contractPublished` endpoint returns CONTRACT-PUBLISHED (award-stage) OCDS releases, where the substantive data lives in `contracts[0]` (title/description/value/items) and `parties[]`, NOT in `tender.*` (which carries only id/procurementMethod) and NOT in `buyer` (null on this feed). The mapping therefore prefers `contracts.0.*` (title, description, value.amount/currency, items.0.classification.id) with `tender.*` fallbacks - confirmed live to yield real contract titles/values/UNSPSC codes rather than fallbacks. (2) `organisation` maps `buyer.name`, which is null on the contract-published feed: the procuring entity sits in `parties[]` behind a role filter (`roles` contains 'buyer'/'procuringEntity') that a declarative index-only dot-path cannot search - so `organisation` lands empty on this feed (parties.0 is the SUPPLIER, not the buyer, so it is deliberately NOT used to avoid mislabeling). A documented, honest gap, not silently wrong. (3) `cpvCodes` reads `contracts.0.items.0.classification.id` (bare dot-path + cast:array, the scalar->single-element trick slovenia_ocds.json/latvia_iub.json document) - AusTender uses UNSPSC codes not CPV, and a declarative dot-path reaches only the first item of the first contract (best-effort single code). (4) `closingDate` (submission deadline) has no field on this award-stage feed (tender.tenderPeriod is absent) - left empty. (5) award data (winner/awarded value) lives inline in `awards[]`/`contracts[]` but cannot be fanned out to separate spectr `tenderAward` objects: the declarative sync is one-source-object -> one-target-object and cannot emit N award children per release, nor resolve the parent tender's not-yet-assigned OR uuid at ingest time - so awards are left unmapped (tenderAward stays at 0 objects, as it is repo-wide). The script's own CPV/UNSPSC/keyword IT filter is its DB-side classification layer, NOT an API constraint (same as TenderNed/TED) - this connector ingests the full unfiltered feed. LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-07 on the isolated spectr-spike instance (NC 34, OR 0.2.17-unstable.13, OC 0.2.16+#105, spectr register id=8) with a narrow date window - see connectors/README.md's W2 table and IMPORT.md for the run evidence (rows, field spot-check, dedup re-run).

objects.name: AusTender (Australian Government procurement)
objects.description: Australian federal procurement OCDS API (api.tenders.gov.au/ocds). Public, unauthenticated OCDS release feed. Feeds the spectr `tender` register/schema via the australia-austender-to-spectr-tender synchronization.

objects.name: AusTender to Spectr Tender
objects.description: Maps a raw AusTender OCDS release onto the spectr `tender` schema. Mirrors sync_australia_austender.py's upsert_tender() field selection. Optional/sometimes-missing OCDS fields are Twig-wrapped with |default('') per IMPORT.md's literal-leak gotcha; cpvCodes is a bare dot-path + cast:array (best-effort single UNSPSC code, see file $comment).

objects.name: AusTender to Spectr Tender
objects.description: Wave-2 ingestion sync: AusTender findByDates/contractPublished for the last 7 days (endpoint computes the ISO date window fresh on every run via self-contained Twig date expressions, no external data needed) -> spectr register, tender schema. `resultsPosition: 'releases'` (OCDS release-package envelope). `usesPagination: false` - the date-window endpoint returns one whole package per call; date-axis coverage comes from the weekly Job cadence, not a page counter.

objects.name: AusTender Weekly Sync
objects.description: Runs the australia-austender-to-spectr-tender synchronization weekly, matching Specter's own tendril cadence. Each run fetches the last 7 days of released notices; the synchronization-contract-keyed upsert (same mechanism tenderned.json relies on) dedups overlap on re-run.
